subject: Mathematics
tagline: Numbers, algebra, geometry, measurement, trigonometry, statistics and probability.
source_note: Curriculum-informed notes supplied for SomaSmart. Confirm the current official grade-specific design with KICD.

strands.name: Numbers and Operations
notes: Natural numbers, integers, rational and irrational numbers; place value up to billions; operations follow BODMAS order.
Factors and multiples: prime factorisation, GCD/HCF and LCM by factor tree or division; divisibility tests for 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11.
Fractions, decimals and percentages: conversion, ratio, proportion (direct and inverse), rates, percentage increase and decrease, and mixtures.
Squares, square roots, cubes and cube roots by factorisation and tables; indices laws and standard form.
Logarithms: product, quotient and power laws; use of logarithm tables and calculators.
Approximation and errors: rounding off, significant figures, absolute, relative and percentage error, and limits of accuracy in sums and products.

strands.name: Algebra
notes: Algebraic expressions: substitution, simplification, expansion, factorisation and algebraic fractions.
Linear equations and inequalities in one and two unknowns; simultaneous equations solved by substitution, elimination and graphically.
Quadratic expressions and equations solved by factorisation, completing the square, the quadratic formula and graphically; the discriminant determines the nature of roots.
Formulae: change of subject, forming equations from word problems, and simple linear programming to maximise or minimise an objective function.
Sequences and series: arithmetic and geometric progressions; compound interest, appreciation and depreciation.
Matrices: order, operations, identity matrix, determinant and inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix, and solving simultaneous equations by matrix method.

strands.name: Measurement and Geometry
notes: Length, area and volume: perimeter and area of plane figures, surface area and volume of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres; frustums by subtraction of similar solids.
Circle measurement: arc length, area of sector, segment and chord properties; angle at centre, angles in the same segment, cyclic quadrilaterals and tangents.
Angles and polygons: parallel lines, interior and exterior angle properties, construction with ruler and compasses, and regular polygons.
Similarity and congruence: SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS; area and volume scale factors; enlargement with positive, negative and fractional scale factors.
Transformations: reflection, rotation, translation, enlargement, shear, stretch, transformation matrices, invariant points and loci.
Pythagoras' theorem in two and three dimensions; latitude, longitude, great circles, distances in nautical miles and time differences.

strands.name: Trigonometry, Vectors and Coordinate Geometry
notes: Trigonometric ratios sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse and tan θ = opposite/adjacent; special angles and bearings.
Trigonometric identities sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and tan θ = sin θ ÷ cos θ; graphs of sine, cosine and tangent.
Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area formula; bearings and three-figure notation in navigation problems.
Vectors: representation, magnitude, addition and subtraction, scalar multiplication, position vectors, midpoint, section formula, collinearity and ratio theorem.
Coordinate geometry: gradient, line equations, parallel and perpendicular lines, distance and midpoint formulae.

strands.name: Statistics and Probability
notes: Data collection and presentation: frequency tables, bar graphs, pie charts, line graphs, histograms, frequency polygons and cumulative frequency curves.
Measures of central tendency: mean, median and mode, including assumed mean and grouped data methods; effect of extreme values.
Measures of dispersion: range, interquartile range, quartiles, percentiles, mean absolute deviation, variance and standard deviation.
Probability: experimental and theoretical probability, mutually exclusive and independent events, tree diagrams and conditional probability.
Interpretation and honest reporting of data, including misleading graphs and sampling bias.

strands.name: Calculus and Applications
notes: Rates of change and gradients of curves; differentiation of polynomials.
Applications of differentiation: gradients, tangents and normals, stationary points, velocity and acceleration from displacement.
Integration as reverse differentiation; definite integrals for area under a curve and volume of revolution basics.
Numerical methods: area estimation by the trapezium rule and mid-ordinate rule; comparison with exact integration.
Real-life applications: profit and cost optimisation, motion problems, growth and decay, and graphs to solve equations approximately.

questions: Simplify (2x² − 8) ÷ (x² + x − 6) and state the values of x for which the expression is undefined.
Solve the simultaneous equations 3x + 2y = 16 and 5x − y = 18 by elimination, then check graphically.
A cone of base radius 7 cm and height 24 cm is cut parallel to the base halfway up. Find the volume of the frustum (take π = 22/7).
Two ships leave a port; A sails 40 km on a bearing of 060° and B sails 55 km on a bearing of 150°. Calculate the distance between them using the cosine rule.
The marks of 50 learners are grouped in classes of width 10 from 30 to 79. Draw an ogive and estimate the median and interquartile range.
A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. Draw a tree diagram and find the probability that both are the same colour.
Find the coordinates of the turning points of y = x³ − 3x² − 9x + 5 and state their nature.
Estimate the area under y = x² + 1 between x = 0 and x = 4 using the trapezium rule with 4 strips, then compare with the exact value by integration.
worked: Factorise the numerator: 2x² − 8 = 2(x − 2)(x + 2).
Factorise the denominator: x² + x − 6 = (x + 3)(x − 2).
Cancel the common factor: the expression simplifies to 2(x + 2) ÷ (x + 3).
The original denominator is zero when x = −3 or x = 2, so it is undefined at these values.
Label the equations 3x + 2y = 16 and 5x − y = 18.
Multiply the second equation by 2: 10x − 2y = 36.
Add the equations: 13x = 52, so x = 4.
Substitute x = 4: 12 + 2y = 16, so y = 2. The lines meet at (4, 2).
Volume of the whole cone = ⅓ × 22/7 × 7² × 24 = 1,232 cm³.
The smaller cone has scale factor ½, so its volume is 1,232 × (½)³ = 154 cm³.
Volume of the frustum = 1,232 − 154 = 1,078 cm³.
The angle between the two courses is 150° − 060° = 90°.
AB = √4,625 = 68.0 km to 3 significant figures.
Using frequencies 4, 8, 14, 16 and 8, cumulative frequencies are 4, 12, 26, 42 and 50.
The median is the 25th value: 49.5 + ((25 − 12) ÷ 14) × 10 = 58.8 marks.
The lower quartile is about 49.9 and upper quartile about 66.7, so the interquartile range is about 16.8 marks.
P(blue then blue) = 3/8 × 2/7 = 6/56.
The outcomes are mutually exclusive, so P(same colour) = 26/56 = 13/28 ≈ 0.464.
Stationary points occur at x = 3 and x = −1.
The points are (3, −22) and (−1, 10). The second derivative identifies (3, −22) as a minimum and (−1, 10) as a maximum.
With 4 strips, h = 1 and the ordinates are 1, 2, 5, 10 and 17.
Trapezium estimate = ½[(1 + 17) + 2(2 + 5 + 10)] = 26 square units.
Exact area = ∫₀⁴(x² + 1)dx = 76/3 ≈ 25.33 square units, so the estimate overstates by about 0.67.
